channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Fed to Soon Consider Raising Bank Asset Thresholds, Bowman Says
item.description: Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman said the Fed will look later this year to update its rules for fixed-dollar asset thresholds in a bid to account for inflation and economic growth. “This will preserve the policy intent at the time the threshold was implemented,” Bowman said Tuesday in remarks to a community banking research conference. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Oaktree’s Playbook for Rising Credit Stress
item.description: As higher rates bite and SEC scrutiny rises, Danielle Poli, a Managing Director and Co-Portfolio Manager at Oaktree, joins Bloomberg Open Interest to break down where credit risk is really building, and where the best opportunities are. From complex data-center deals to looming refinancings and distressed software names, she explains how smart credit investors are positioning. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Inside the Toys "R" Us Comeback
item.description: WHP Global is bringing Toys "R" Us back to life with over 120 new US stores despite falling consumer confidence. Yehuda Shmidman, the founder, chairman and CEO of the brand licensing company WHP Global, joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why toy demand is surging, the rise of the “kidult” shopper, and how an asset‑light licensing model is powering billions in sales and potential IPO plans. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tech Tries to Power Stocks to Fresh Records Despite Elevated Yields
item.description: Jonathan Ferro, Lisa Abramowicz and Annmarie Hordern speak daily with leaders and decision makers from Wall Street to Washington and beyond. No other program better positions investors and executives for the trading day than "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Russia’s Oil-Export Boom Undercut by Payouts, Diesel Sales Ban
item.description: Diesel curbs, jump in subsidies to refiners mute benefits to Kremlin’s war chest from crude flows
item.dc:creator: Julian Lee

item.title: French Fiscal Concerns Bring Home Painful Risk Premium
item.description: After decades of budget deficits and steadily rising debt, markets are putting a new price on French risk. Investors are charging much more to hold government bonds, the stock market is under pressure and the cost of insuring bank bonds against default has jumped. The euro fell to its weakest level since May 2025 on Monday, reflecting fears that upheaval will spill beyond France’s border. Ozan Tarman, Vice Chair: Global Macro at Deutsche Bank, discusses the growing debt pressures across Europe and contagion risks. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says “Threats” Forced US To Move Bombers From UK Base
item.description:
President Trump says "threats" forced the US to withdraw its B-1B bombers from RAF Fairford, a UK airbase at the center of a terrorism investigation.
Gerry Doyle explains what we know. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Francia paga por décadas de déficits fiscales y crisis
item.description: París enfrenta una factura creciente por su deuda justo cuando la política dificulta una solución. Los mercados se preparan para una volatilidad que podría prolongarse hasta las elecciones.
item.dc:creator: George Nixon, Julien Ponthus and Tasos Vossos

item.title: Venture Global Is in Talks to Sell US LNG to More Chinese Buyers
item.description: US liquefied natural gas exporter Venture Global Inc. is in talks to sell the fuel to additional Chinese buyers as the Iran war roils global shipments, spurring China to seek to diversify its sources of supply.
item.dc:creator: Sing Yee Ong, Ruth Liao and Stephen Stapczynski

item.title: Ares Faces 50% Loss on Money It Piled Into TalkTalk With BT Deal
item.description: Ares Management Corp is set to lose about half of the hundreds of millions of pounds it invested in TalkTalk, after BT Group Plc agreed to buy the telecommunications firm out of insolvency.
item.dc:creator: Giulia Morpurgo

item.title: Quebec Bonds Tighten as Separatist Party Falls Short of Majority
item.description: The separatist Parti Québécois won Quebec’s election but fell short of a majority government, a result that’s boosting investor confidence in the province’s bonds.
item.dc:creator: Chunzi Xu

item.title: Google, Constellation Energy Deal; SpaceX Rises on Talks with NASA | Stock Movers
item.description:
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- Option Care Health (OPCH) shares jumped after the Financial Times reports that McKesson and PE firm Clayton Dubilier & Rice are closing in on a deal to buy the provider of medical infusion services, that would value the business at more than $5b including debt. - Constellation Energy (CEG) shares are higher on news Google and Constellation Energy announced a long-term deal to bring 890 MW of new nuclear capacity on the PJM grid in Illinois, Pennsylvania and New Jersey. - SpaceX (SPCX) shares are the most actively traded in the premarket as NASA is close to announcing a bulk purchase of rocket launches to fuel its $30 billion drive to build a permanent base on the moon for humans to live and work. It also made Elon Musk a trillionaire once again. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Google, Constellation Energy Strike Nuclear Power Deal
item.description: Google parent Alphabet Inc. agreed to buy nuclear power from Constellation Energy in a 20-year power-purchase agreement that will drive more than $4.3 billion in investments to upgrade systems at 11 Constellation reactors. Ed Ludlow has more on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dimon Says If You Try to Game the Market, You'll Lose
item.description: JPMorgan Chase & Co. Chief Executive Officer Jamie Dimon says investors should get used to the fact that markets go up and down. He says if you try to game the market, you are guaranteed to lose money. He speaks exclusively with Tom Mackenzie at JPMorgan’s Tech Stars Conference in London. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: S&P 500 Sets First Record Since August as Bulls Downplay Risk
item.description: The S&P 500 rose 0.9%, reaching its first record high since August, buoyed by resilient corporate profits, the outlook for artificial intelligence-related spending and a pullback in oil prices.
item.dc:creator: Natalia Kniazhevich and Jan-Patrick Barnert

item.title: Paulsen Sees a 15% S&P 500 Drop as Oil, Rates and Dollar Rise
item.description: The higher the wall of worry, the faster US stocks have climbed it, clocking its first record since August on Tuesday. But to Jim Paulsen, the cumulative pressure from $100 oil prices, 5% Treasury yields and an elevated dollar is yet to be felt in a major way.
item.dc:creator: Geoffrey Morgan

item.title: Air Liquide Sells Debt at Better Rate Than French Government
item.description: Air Liquide SA attracted strong demand for a sale of euro-denominated bonds, with investors buying the debt at lower yields than French government bonds caught up in the country’s fiscal and political turmoil.
item.dc:creator: Ronan Martin and Abraham Gonzalez

item.title: S&P 500 Hits All-Time High on AI Bets as Oil Drops: Markets Wrap
item.description: A pullback in oil prices sent stocks to all-time highs, with Wall Street also buoyed by renewed enthusiasm about the artificial-intelligence trade that has powered the bull market.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 6
item.description: Oil slipped on rising exports from the Middle East, with more Gulf producers moving large volumes through the Strait of Hormuz despite still-elevated risks from the Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Kanoko Matsuyama and Paul Burkhardt

item.title: Airbnb’s Bet on Experience-Driven Marketing
item.description: Airbnb Chief Experience Officer Hiroki Asai explains how the company seeks to drive deeper brand engagement through real-world experiences. (Source: Bloomberg)
